subject: Skyhook model intake: compatibility playbook + provisional version hold
messages:
From: Elana Gomez <elana@skyhook.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Skyhook model intake: compatibility checklist + provisional pin request

Hi Laura / Rishi / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on — I'm Elana (Head of Partnerships, Skyhook AI). We're aiming to onboard a new model variant (skyhook-13b-v1) into Redwood Hosted so some of our pilot customers can test it behind a controlled rollout. Before we start the formal intake, two asks:

1) A short compatibility checklist we can work through with your infra and ops teams (tokenizer, kv-cache expectations, custom ops).
2) A provisional version hold (temporary pin) during the initial canary window so we can stabilize outputs while telemetry is collected. We propose 6 weeks but we're flexible to Redwood's process.

What I'm attaching: model manifest (lightweight), a sample of inference requests (to approximate seq len/QPS), and an initial safety self-check report.

Attachments: skyhook-v1-manifest.json (manifest), poc-sample-requests.json (samples)

Ideal timeline from our side: onboard intakes this week -> staging canary by next Tue -> controlled host rollout the following week. Happy to sync on a quick 30m call.

Quick context: skyhook-13b uses a slightly modified byte-level tokenizer (small prefix tokens) and a fused attention kernel for improved density. We expect 90th pct token length ~600, median 200. Expected pilot QPS: 8-12 across 50 concurrent users.

Thanks — Elana
Skyhook AI
+1 415 555 0134

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elana Gomez <elana@skyhook.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyhook model intake: compatibility checklist + provisional pin request

Elana — thanks for the detailed note and the artifacts, appreciate the seq/QPS numbers. Putting together next steps so we have a single coordination thread:

- Intake owner: Laura Bennett (me) — I'll shepherd the intake and approval steps.
- Runtime perf: Rishi will validate kernel/quantization implications and run a quick perf sweep on a representative instance.
- Rollouts/pin policy: Kimberly will evaluate whether a provisional pin is acceptable and for how long given routing and fallback tooling.
- Safety & evals: We'll run our standard mini-eval (toxicity/regressions) but we may need a short extra pass because of the tokenizer tweak.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Confirm a checksum for the model bundle (SHA256) and whether there are any non-open kernels (we need build licensing details).
- Provide a single canonical invocation example (we'll use the attached sample as a baseline).

Proposed process and timing:
1) Today: compat triage (we'll kick off infra + evals).
2) Within 3 business days: perf and safety findings + recommended pin length.
3) If acceptable: provisional pin + canary plan (we'll propose canary routes and telemetry gates).

Can we do a 30m sync at 11:30am PT today? Here's a calendar link: https://calendar.redwood.com/laura/30m (feel free to propose another time).

Thanks — I'll loop back as soon as Rishi has perf numbers.

— Laura Bennett
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Elana Gomez <elana@skyhook.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyhook model intake: compatibility checklist + provisional pin request

Quick datapoints from infra perspective (initial read):

- Tokenizer: a "byte-prefix" tweak can be handled if you provide tokenizer.json and vocab files. We'll validate that tokenization mapping doesn't dramatically shift token counts compared to byte-level baseline. If there are reserved special tokens, call that out.
- KV cache: expected 600 tokens 90th pct — memory lookups will be the dominant factor. We need a representative sequence (you sent samples; thanks).
- Kernels: if your fused attention uses a custom CUDA op we must vet the binary and licensing. If it's a standard matmul/attention path with operator-level fusions, we can run with existing kernels.

Can you confirm the following so I can run perf sims:
- Typical prompt+response average token lengths (we have sample but want an average metric).
- Expected concurrent sessions and burst QPS (you mentioned 8-12, confirm expected peak).

I've attached a perf-run-template.csv — please fill the averages and return. I'll schedule a short perf sweep (approx 2–4 hours) on a c6g-style test harness and share results. Preliminary estimate: if no custom ops and quantization works to int8 without significant quality regression, throughput should be within 20% of our standard 13B baselines.

Attachment: perf-run-template.csv

— Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Elana Gomez <elana@skyhook.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyhook model intake: compatibility checklist + provisional pin request

Marking up the pin question from policy/ops side:

We can accept a provisional version hold under the following conditions:
1) Max provisional window: 3 weeks (not 6). We find shorter windows reduce long-lived operational debt and encourage faster telemetry-driven decisions.
2) Required artifacts before pin: SHA256 of model bundle, tokenizer files, signed statement about any non-standard CUDA binaries.
3) Rollback/runbook: Skyhook must provide a rollback runbook template we can incorporate; Redwood needs an automated fallback route defined (which model to route to if issues appear).
4) Telemetry gates: latency 95th pct and regression in our eval set (we'll share baseline) — both must be within agreed thresholds to extend the pin.

I've filed an intake ticket SUP-3421 and added a short checklist. Link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-3421

If you meet items 1–3, I'm comfortable approving a 3-week provisional hold and a staged canary. We'll re-evaluate at day 10 with telemetry.

I'll draft a minimal rollback-runbook-template.md and attach it here for Skyhook to fill.

— Kimberly Park
Lead, Product Security & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Elana Gomez <elana@skyhook.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyhook model intake: compatibility checklist + provisional pin request

Thanks all — appreciate the thoroughness and quick turnaround. We can comply with the conditions. Action items from Skyhook:

- We'll provide SHA256 for the model bundle and upload tokenizer.json + vocab.txt within 1 business day.
- We'll confirm kernel licensing (our fused attention is open-source licensed under MIT; no proprietary blobs).
- We'll fill the perf-run-template.csv with average prompt/response lengths and expected peak QPS by tomorrow 10am PT.
- We'll complete the rollback-runbook-template.md and return it.

We agree to the 3-week provisional pin with the day-10 review. We also confirm SUP-3421 as the intake ticket — we'll add Skyhook artifacts as attachments there and assign our lead eng (cc: tech-lead@skyhook.ai).

Plan: Laura — once you confirm the staging slot we'll kick off the perf sweep.

— Elana
Head of Partnerships, Skyhook AI
